paragraphs.text: Deterministic, one-way PII anonymizer at the start of the DeepSeek Harness agent loop
# dsh-pii-anonymizer

A native DeepSeek Harness plugin
that replaces **detected PII with stable placeholders in what the m

odel is sent**:
your prompt, the system prompt, runtime context, workspace instructions, recalled
se
ssions, relayed agent messages, and tool results.

Detection uses fixed rules and checksums (never a model). Every detected value is
replaced with a ke

yed placeholder such as `[[EMAIL_3f9a2c1d]]` before the request
goes to the provider. The real value

s do stay on this computer: the host app
commits your message to the local session log exactly as yo

u typed it, and files
and tool outputs on disk are not changed.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The notice is a **user-role message**: it is shown in your transcript *and* the
model receives it (t

hat is how the harness delivers plugin notices). It carries
only types and counts — never values or

placeholders. Turn it off with
`notify: false`.

Anonymization is **one-way**: the plugin keeps no value → placeholder table and
has no restore path,
so nothing it holds can put the real values back.
## Where it hooks

Each listener is registered with `prepend: true`, so it is the outermost
listener of its waterfall a

nd rewrites the final value after every other plugin
has contributed.
| Hook (package) | What is rewritten |
| `system-prompt/assemble` (`dsh-system-prompt`) | prompt **section** text (e.g. a terminal app's wo
rkspace section), runtime-**context** text, and string prompt **variables**. The agent loop renders
the assembled contexts into its `form: "snapshot"` user message, so snapshots (e.g. a memory index)

are covered here, and the loop's "has the snapshot changed?" check stays stable. |
| `agent/pre-step
` (`dsh-agent-loop`) | the text blocks of **every** message entering the step, whatever its source:
the user prompt, runtime-context snapshots, workspace instructions (`AGENTS.md`), recalled sessions
(`recall`), relayed agent messages (`relay`), skill catalogs, and contexts attached by tool results.

|
| `tools/post-execute` (`dsh-tools`) | the tool **result content** the model reads (file reads, g
rep, shell output, memory reads…), a block decision's feedback, and attached contexts. |
### Why a native plugin, not a hook

The Claude Code / Codex hook bridges **cannot** do this. `HookOutput` in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-hook-prot

ocol` exposes only `additionalContext`; its
`updatedInput` is documented as *"PARSED but NOT honored

."* There is no
prompt-rewrite channel. Only a native Cordis plugin can replace the messages,
prompt
, and tool results that enter the model request.
## Detection scope

Deterministic means *structural*. The detectors find things with a grammar or a
checksum:
| Type | Trigger | Validation |
| `API_KEY` | known prefixes (`sk-`, `sk-ant-`, `AKIA…`, `ghp_…`, `github_pat_…`, `xox…`, `AIza…`) |

— |
| `IBAN` | `CC00…`, compact or space-grouped | **mod-97 checksum** |
| `CREDIT_CARD` | 13–19 di

gits, spaces/dashes allowed | **Luhn checksum** |
| `SSN` | `DDD-DD-DDDD` | none |
| `EMAIL` | RFC-i

sh address shape | none |
| `IPV6` / `IPV4` | address shapes | octet range for IPv4 |
| `PHONE` | di
git run with `+ ( ) . - space`, optional leading `(`, 7–15 digits | rejects ISO dates and version st
with `+ ( ) . - space`, optional leading `(`, 7–15 digits | rejects ISO dates and version strings |

Free-form **names, postal addresses, and other context-dependent PII are not
detected** — a determin

istic rule cannot catch them without unacceptable false
positives. Adding an ML/NER stage would brea
k the "deterministic" property.

Overlaps are resolved by priority (checksum types beat the loose phone rule),
then span length, then

re resolved by priority (checksum types beat the loose phone rule),
then span length, then position.
## Pseudonymization model

A placeholder is `[[TYPE_<hash>]]`, where `<hash>` is the first 8 hex digits of
HMAC-SHA256(key, typ

e + normalized value). Normalization folds trivial spelling
differences (email case, IBAN/card/phone
spacing and separators) into one value.

- **Stable everywhere.** The same value gets the same placeholder in every
[该节后续省略]
## What is and is not covered
Covered (model-facing text):

- your prompt and every other message entering a step — snapshots, workspace
instructions, recall, r

elay, catalogs, tool-result contexts;
- system-prompt sections, runtime-context sections, and string

prompt variables;
- tool result content, including errors returned by a tool body.
Not covered:

- **Local storage.** The session log, transcript, memory files, and any file on
disk keep the raw va

lues; this shield changes only what is sent to the
provider. The raw values are protected by the fil

e permissions of `$DSH_HOME`
and nothing else.
- **Undetectable PII.** Free-form names, postal addre

sses, and other
context-dependent PII are not detected (see *Detection scope*).
- **A `complete: tru

e` system-prompt section.** `dsh-system-prompt` restores an
effective complete section from its pre-

waterfall text *after* the
`system-prompt/assemble` waterfall, so a plugin cannot rewrite it.
- **To

ol schemas** (tool names, descriptions, parameter schemas) are sent as is.
- **Tool results that ski

p `tools/post-execute`.** The registry finalizes a
few outcomes without post-execute — cancellations

and pipeline failures (for
example a throwing `tools/pre-execute` or `tools/execute` listener) — an

d a
tool's own `finalizeContent` callback runs after post-execute. Their text
reaches the model unre

written. Denials, approval rejections, tool errors and
successes all pass through post-execute and a

re covered. A downstream
post-execute listener that replaces the result's `value` is left alone (the

registry forbids replacing both value and content).
- **Model output.** The assistant's replies are

not rewritten; placeholders are
not restored in them.
- **Requests made outside the agent loop** by

other plugins (for example a
session-title generator) only see what the loop already rewrote — the

title
request built from your messages receives the placeholders, but a plugin that
reads raw files
itself and calls a model directly is outside this shield.

Rewriting injected context can occasionally hide a value the agent genuinely
needs (for example an I

P address in a workspace instruction). Disable the
[该节后续省略]
